domain_guidance.summary: This specific domain covers physical and biological anthropology topics representing exactly 13.0 percent of the overall examination content, requiring study of human biological variation, primate behavior and evolution, and the hominin fossil record.

This particular domain focuses on archaeology concepts accounting for exactly 10.0 percent of the total exam weight, requiring mastery of excavation and survey methods, artifact analysis and dating techniques, and methods for reconstructing past societies.

This content domain explores linguistic anthropology topics including language structure, historical evolution, and social use, focusing on the intersections of language and culture, sociolinguistic variations, and various forms of non-verbal communication.

This domain examines fundamental cultural anthropology concepts such as complex social structures, diverse belief systems, and human organization, paying close attention to kinship and family systems, economic and political structures, as well as religion and ritual practices.

faq.answer_text: The exam consists of exactly 100 multiple-choice questions delivered entirely in a computer-based format designed to test your knowledge across four distinct subfields of anthropology.

faq.answer_text: The minimum passing score required to successfully earn college credit for this examination is set at a standardized score of 400 for all test takers.
Test-takers participating in this certification process are given a total time limit of 120 minutes to complete all of the computer-based multiple-choice questions contained within the test format.
The standard exam price is $85 for civilians, whereas eligible military personnel can take the test completely free of charge through funding provided via DANTES.

editorial.overview: The DSST General Anthropology examination is professionally administered by DSST and covers physical and biological anthropology, archaeology, linguistic anthropology, and cultural anthropology in extensive detail. It provides a computer-based multiple-choice format consisting of exactly 100 questions. Candidates are given precisely 120 minutes to complete the test successfully and demonstrate their comprehensive knowledge.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Carefully review core concepts across all four major anthropological subfields to ensure complete readiness for the examination. Practice extensively with multiple-choice questions to build necessary test-taking speed for the 100-question format within the strict 120-minute limit. Check directly with DSST for study resources and registration details.
editorial.who_should_take: This certification exam perfectly suits students seeking college credit for introductory anthropology knowledge. Eligible military personnel can take it completely free via DANTES, while regular civilians pay the standard fee of $85.
